transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-19
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Ruiz (Redwood SE), Hana Lee (Redwood SE), Alicia Chen (KiteField VP Eng), Marco Oliveira (KiteField ML Eng), Priya Rao (KiteField Infra Lead), Samir Gupta (KiteField Product)

Summary:
Quick alignment on POC success criteria with emphasis on hybrid SLOs: first-token latency (TTFT) targets for interactive UX and total-token throughput (TPOT) targets for batch/async endpoint; define sampling plan, measurement method, and a 2-week benchmark window.

Topics covered:
- Business success criteria and stakeholders
- TTFT vs TPOT tradeoffs and which endpoints matter
- Target p95/p99 goals and how they map to UX vs cost constraints
- Traffic profile sampling and payload variance (short prompts vs long context)
- Measurement harness, warm-up, KV cache behavior, burstiness and autoscale considerations
- Timeline and responsibilities

Action items (recap at end included above): see action_items field

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call and then we'll jump into goals, um, for the POC.
[00:12] Alicia (KiteField): Hi all, Alicia here. We, yeah, we want to validate both responsiveness for our chat UI and cost/throughput for batch summarization.
[00:20] Jonah (Redwood SE): Great. Just to set expectations, typical POC cadence is: define SLOs, run controlled bench, iterate on model variant and batch/quant profiles, then hand off runbook.
[00:31] Priya (KiteField): For infra constraints, we need to be explicit about private deployment options — some data stays in VPC — and also about cold-start behavior.
[00:41] Hana (Redwood SE): Noted. We'll include a VPC test plan. For cold start, are you referring to container spin-up or KV cache warm state?
[00:49] Priya (KiteField): Both. For interactive sessions we care more about first token after a user prompt, for nightly batches it's total tokens per second.
[00:58] Marco (KiteField): Quick note: our chat average prompt length is 22 tokens, but we have a long-tail with 6% > 1024 tokens — those are the expensive ones.
[01:08] Jonah (Redwood SE): That's helpful. For the POC we usually separate traffic into short, medium, long buckets and sample accordingly.
[01:16] Samir (KiteField): From product side we want 95th percentile snappy responses — users shouldn't wait more than ~300ms for the first token in typical flows.
[01:25] Maya (Redwood AE): Good concrete number — 300ms p95 for TTFT on interactive endpoints. Is that for hosted or dedicated?
[01:33] Samir (KiteField): Both ideally, but we'd accept a slightly higher p95 for our private deployment if necessary.
[01:40] Alicia (KiteField): For batch summarization the throughput target is more important — we're looking at TPOT measured as tokens/sec at p95 under steady-state. Current infra baseline is ~18k tokens/sec for their in-house setup but with higher latency variance.
[01:53] Jonah (Redwood SE): Ok. Two separate SLOs then: TTFT p95/p99 for interactive endpoints and TPOT p95 for batch endpoints. We should pick p99 numbers too for safety, maybe TTFT p99 <= 600ms?
[02:05] Marco (KiteField): p99 600ms seems reasonable as a guardrail. For batch, we usually watch p95 throughput and tail latencies on large payloads, so maybe TPOT p95 >= 15k tokens/sec as an initial target.
[02:18] Hana (Redwood SE): We'll propose a matrix: short prompt TTFT p95 300ms / p99 600ms; medium prompt TTFT p95 450ms / p99 900ms; TPOT baseline p95 15k tokens/sec for the batch profile — those are starting points.
[02:33] Priya (KiteField): How will we measure first-token correctly? Our traces are only at app layer.
[02:39] Jonah (Redwood SE): Good question. Measurement plan: instrument at the SDK client for TTFT (timestamp request send vs first token received) and also at Redwood routing layer for server-side verification. For TPOT we measure server-side token emission rates and end-to-end from client to final token as well. We'll share scripts.
[02:56] Alicia (KiteField): Any gotchas on KV cache? Sometimes the local KV warms on earlier requests and makes first-token very fast — skewing the numbers.
[03:05] Jonah (Redwood SE): Exactly. We'll include cold/warm buckets in the sampling plan. For the POC benchmark we'll run both a cold-start sweep and a sustained steady-state run with pre-warm steps. Also need to account for continuous batching effects.
[03:19] Marco (KiteField): Continuous batching — does Redwood's runtime combine different users into batches? That could affect tail latencies.
[03:25] Hana (Redwood SE): Yes, Redwood runtime does workload-aware batching. For POC measurement we can control concurrency and batch windows to reproduce production-like batching. We'll provide harness knobs.
[03:36] Samir (KiteField): We're sensitive to cost; if we push batch sizes high to get token/sec we're also paying more GPU time. Can you show cost impact in the runbook?
[03:45] Maya (Redwood AE): Absolutely. One POC output will be a cost vs latency tradeoff table across quantization and batching configs.
[03:52] Priya (KiteField): On security: we need explicit confirmation of audit logs for private deployment and KMS integration for key management.
[03:59] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll attach the SOC2 and KMS integration docs. Hana, can you follow up on encryption and audit log details?
[04:06] Hana (Redwood SE): Yes, I'll share the private deployment checklist and a sample audit log export.
[04:12] Marco (KiteField): About traffic shaping: are we going to replay traces or synthetic load?
[04:18] Jonah (Redwood SE): Both. Replay real traces for fidelity and synthetic bursts to test autoscale and tail behavior. We recommend a replay at 1x production then scaled runs at 2x/5x for stress.
[04:28] Alicia (KiteField): Timeline — we're aiming to decide vendor by end of Feb, so we need the benchmark results by mid-Feb. Is that realistic?
[04:36] Maya (Redwood AE): If we get traces by Jan 23 and set up the test account the week of Jan 29 we can run benchmarks Feb 1-7 and deliver results Feb 10-12. That fits your decision window.
[04:47] Samir (KiteField): Great. We also want a short demo of SLO dashboards and per-token cost breakdown during the benchmark review.
[04:55] Hana (Redwood SE): Yep we'll include the Console views: per-route latency, per-token cost, and sampling breakdowns.
[05:02] Marco (KiteField): Measurement specifics — do you recommend measuring TTFT as client-measured or server measured?
[05:08] Jonah (Redwood SE): Client measurement is the source of truth for UX. Server-side measurement verifies internal behavior and helps explain deltas. We'll include sync points to correlate spans.
[05:18] Priya (KiteField): Also want to track p50/p90 for completeness, but the decision will be p95/p99.
[05:24] Maya (Redwood AE): Noted. We'll include p50/p90 in the benchmark artifact, but SLOs will be p95/p99 for TTFT and p95 for TPOT.
[05:33] Samir (KiteField): Edge case — long documents >1024 tokens. How do you measure token emission rate there?
[05:38] Jonah (Redwood SE): For long-form we measure token emission rate over sliding windows; we report initial generation slope and steady-state tokens/sec. We'll capture both as part of TPOT metrics.
[05:46] Alicia (KiteField): For acceptance: what would qualify Redwood as pass?
[05:50] Maya (Redwood AE): Proposed acceptance criteria: 1) Interactive endpoints meet TTFT p95 target for short/medium buckets within 10% of target; 2) Batch endpoints deliver TPOT p95 within 15% of target at comparable cost; 3) No unacceptably high p99 spikes during steady-state tests; 4) Security and VPC checklist satisfied.
[06:07] Marco (KiteField): Ok, percent leeway is good. We'll define exact pass/fail thresholds in the SLO doc.
[06:12] Hana (Redwood SE): We'll also include a risk register for known gaps — e.g., tail behavior under extreme burstiness, or quantization artifacts impacting quality.
[06:21] Priya (KiteField): Who from Redwood will run the benchmark? Is it remote or on our private deployment?
[06:27] Jonah (Redwood SE): We can run both. For hosted/Dedicated Redwood can orchestrate the benchmark. For private, we provide the harness and remote assist; Priya's infra team will execute under our guidance.
[06:38] Samir (KiteField): Let's agree on dates now — Marco will share traces by Monday 23rd, Maya will send the SLO draft by 24th, and Jonah will provision harness by 27th. Benchmarks run Feb 1-7. Review Feb 10.
[06:51] Maya (Redwood AE): Perfect. I'll also include an appendix that maps each SLO to the stakeholder who cares (product, infra, biz ops).
[06:58] Alicia (KiteField): One more thing — can you include a small section on graceful degradation strategies? If a model variant is not available, we need automated fallback policies.
[07:06] Hana (Redwood SE): Yes, Redwood supports automated fallback to smaller variants and region-level routing; we'll include expected latency deltas in that scenario.
[07:14] Marco (KiteField): Anything else on sampling? For reproducibility we want seed info and deterministic sampling where possible.
[07:20] Jonah (Redwood SE): Agreed — harness will capture RNG seeds, model revisions, quantization flags, and environment kernels. We'll record those as part of each benchmark run.
[07:31] Priya (KiteField): Ok thanks all.
[07:33] Maya (Redwood AE): Quick recap of next steps and owners — and we'll follow up with the doc and links.
[07:40] Samir (KiteField): Thanks, feel like we're aligned.
[07:43] Maya (Redwood AE): Great — meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
